title: Freeport LNG export terminal: blocked-in 18-inch LNG transfer line (June 2022)
source: PHMSA, Freeport LNG Development, LP, Amended Notice of Probable Violation CPF 4-2024-033-NOPV, 20 December 2024; drawing by PlantAgent; illustrative values where the public record is redacted
question: VIP-18 was isolated for relief-valve testing and left blocked in, partially filled with LNG at 37 psig. What happens to its pressure over the following days, when does it exceed design, and what should have prevented it?
data_note: Facility facts and the timeline up to the second valve closure are from PHMSA's public notice (NOPV, Dec 2024). Segment length, pipe specification, design pressure, LNG composition, fill and heat leak are not public and are marked ILLUSTRATIVE. Tags are illustrative. The slider moves time blocked in, not throughput.
